text:
alice_support: FYI NovaHealth (SUP-8912) hit a blocker. Using streaming chat + fncall -> structured webhook flow and their parser is failing. Our web proxy sometimes delivers two JSON frames back-to-back in one TCP write and their receiver tries to parse as a single JSON object.

bob_sales: They're scheduled to GA tomorrow. this is blocking their launch. they asked for a patch or a clear workaround asap. :sweat_smile:

carol_pm: Can we get the minimal webhook trace + a hex dump? need to know whether this is coalescing at our side or the customer's client.

alice_support: attached in the ticket: payload looks like `{"result":{...}}{"result":{...}}` in one POST body occasionally. Not every request, maybe 1-2% under load.

dave_eng: Quick take: likely two things: (1) our streaming proxy buffers multiple flushes and sends as one request when downstream socket has capacity (Nagle/coalescing), (2) we don't include a separator token or content-length per logical frame when proxying to webhooks.

carol_pm: Triage options:
- Add a stable delimiter between logical frames (e.g. `\n\n--redwood-frame--\n\n`) and document it for webhook consumers (fast, medium risk for backward compat)
- Switch to multipart/form-data or content-length delimited frames when proxying to webhooks (safer, more work)
- Server-side buffer that splits concatenated payloads before forwarding (transparent, but edge-casey)
- Recommend client-side defensive parsing (try parse-second-chunk on error) and call it out in docs (lowest effort)
Which should be hotfix vs backlog?

erin_prodops: For Dedicated/Private we need a release schedule. Hosted can be fast. Any change to payload format needs clear rollout notes and opt-in flag for customers during migration.

dave_eng: Implementation idea: add a tiny separator token emitted immediately after each logical JSON frame in the stream. At proxy time, if we detect contiguous JSON objects we split on that token. Pros: simple, low perf cost. Cons: customers who expect pure JSON must opt-in/parse. I can prototype the separator + split logic in ~1 day.

bob_sales: NovaHealth can accept a short-lived workaround if we give them a clear parsing snippet. They can patch their receiver to split on `}\n{` and re-parse. But they'd prefer a server-side fix.

carol_pm: Acceptance criteria for a Hosted canary fix:
- Reduction of concatenated-frame POSTs to <0.1% in canary region
- Integration test: synthesize two frames and ensure webhook receives two distinct parseable objects when slow downstream applies coalescing
- Monitoring: new metric `webhook.concatenated_frames` and alert at >0.5%
- No increase in p95 latency > 7% in canary region
- Rollback plan and opt-in flag documented in GH PR

alice_support: I'll add the customer's trace and their contact notes to SUP-8912, let them know we're pursuing a canary patch.

erin_prodops: Dave, estimate for prototype + canary rollout? also include Dedicated/private backport estimate.

dave_eng: Prototype + unit tests: ~1.0 engineer-day. Canary + infra + dashboards: ~3 days. Dedicated/private backport/packaging: +2 days.

bob_sales: I'll tell NovaHealth we'll try to get a canary out in 48-72 hours and offer the simple client-side split snippet as a stopgap.

carol_pm: Decision: Hosted canary with separator-splitting approach. Create GH issue GH-4301 `runtime: webhook frame-splitting for streaming fncall flows`. Mark SUP-8912 in-progress and add customer note.

dave_eng: starting prototype, will post PR with tests and a small README with the opt-in header `Redwood-Frame-Splitting: true` to reduce surprise for receivers.

carol_pm: keep thread updates short. if prototype shows perf regression we'll pivot to server-side splitter. Thanks everyone.
